faq.a: Partly. 5 of the 13 versions of Mistral in the OpenRouter catalog publish open weights, and 8 are served over APIs only. The family's repositories on Hugging Face declare the Apache 2.0 licence.
Through the OpenRouter catalog, Mistral costs from $0.03 to $2 per million input tokens and from $0.03 to $7.5 per million output tokens, depending on the version. The cheapest is Mistral Nemo.
Mistral Large 4 is the newest version in the OpenRouter catalog, added on 2026-10-06. The newest dated model line on Mistral AI's own site is Mistral Large 4, dated 2026-10-06.
faq.q: What is the newest Mistral model?

faq.a: Mistral versions accept file, image and text as input and produce text. 3 of the 13 versions support reasoning, and context windows run from 32,768 to 1,048,576 tokens.
Mistral is developed by Mistral AI. Mistral AI is a research lab founded in 2023 and headquartered in Paris, France.

Mistral AI's own site names these ways to use its models: Mistral Priority Tier, Mistral Regional Endpoints, partners, open weights, Mistral Vibe and Hugging Face. In the OpenRouter catalog, 7 providers serve it.

paragraphs: Mistral is a family of AI models from the developer Mistral AI. The pages describe models such as Mistral Large 4, Mistral Medium 3.5, Mistral Small 4, Mistral 3, Mistral OCR 4, Mistral OCR 3, Mistral OCR, Codestral 25.08, Devstral 2, Voxtral, Magistral, Pixtral-12B, Mistral7Bv3, Mistral Large 2407, Shieldstral, Robostral Navigate, and Leanstral 1.5. Mistral AI says these models are for tasks including document intelligence, coding, text to speech, reasoning, image reasoning, and embodied navigation.

The family is organised into sizes and related lines. The pages mention Mistral Large, Mistral Medium, Mistral Small, and Mistral 3, as well as specialised lines for coding, documents, speech, vision, moderation, and physics. Mistral AI offers the models through its API, Studio, Vibe, Le Chat, the Mistral Agents API, and the Finetuning API. Some models are open-weights, and some are available under the Mistral AI Research License or the Mistral AI Non-Production License.

Mistral AI says Mistral OCR 4 is a state of the art document intelligence model, and that Voxtral TTS is a frontier, open-weights text-to-speech model. The pages also state that Mistral AI raised €3 billion in a Series D funding round at a post-money valuation of more than €21 billion, and that it raised 1.7B€ to accelerate technological progress with AI.

price_limits.summary: Across the 13 versions, input prices run from $0.03 to $2 per million tokens and output prices from $0.03 to $7.5. Mistral Nemo is the cheapest, at $0.03 per million input tokens and $0.03 per million output tokens. Mistral Large 4 has the largest context window, 1,048,576 tokens.

family_reading.text: Mistral spans 13 versions, with context windows from 32768 to 524288 tokens and output limits up to 262144. Prices range widely, from $0.02 per million input for Mistral Nemo to $2 for older Large releases, with the newest Large 4 at $0.68 input and $2.09 output. Inputs cover text, image and file, outputs are text only. Across the family, 3 versions support reasoning and 5 publish open weights, so reasoning and open weights are available but not standard. The cheapest open weights options, such as Mistral Small 3 and Nemo, suit high volume, cost sensitive work, while the newest Large and Medium tiers offer long context and reasoning at higher prices. Limits include text only output, and the priciest tiers are costly for heavy use.
